headline: Binance says it has found more weak points behind its roughly $6.3B hack and expects withdrawals back within about 45 hours, forced selling has reached $1.57B, and ICE's Hyperliquid futures plan keeps HYPE rising.

market.asOf: Read from a CoinDesk report published around 11:09 UTC Fri 30 Oct (18:09 Bangkok), not live price pages: CoinGecko, CoinMarketCap and the Fear & Greed index could not be opened this run, and no SOL reading was found. Check the live prices at the top of the page.

stories.title: Binance hack: more breach points found, withdrawals expected back within about 45 hours
stories.summary: Binance says its investigation has uncovered additional points of breach. Withdrawals are still suspended, and Binance expects to resume them in the next 45 hours, per Reuters. It puts the hack at about $6.3B and says about $3B has been located so far; it did not say what happened to the remaining $3.3B.
points: Stablecoin issuers froze about half the stolen assets: Tether nearly $1.57B and Circle more than $800M, per Reuters.
About $2.5B in ether and tokens was gone less than four minutes after a Binance wallet signed an Ethereum permission (EIP-7702) that handed control to another program, per CoinDesk.
About 18,270 BTC (about $1.4B) was split into 19 wallets; as of 04:23 UTC none had moved, and no issuer can freeze bitcoin, per CoinDesk.
TRM Labs and Chainalysis are highly confident North Korea was responsible, per Reuters.

sources.label: Reuters via Yahoo: Tether and Circle freezes

stories.title: Forced selling hits $1.57B as bitcoin dips to $76,400 overnight
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell to an overnight low of $76,400 before winning back some of the drop, and forced closures of trading positions jumped. Options traders are now paying more for protection against further falls.
points: Liquidations reached $1.57B, about four times higher: $522M in bitcoin and $361M in ether, per CoinDesk.
Bitcoin was about $77,350 (down 3.1% in 24 hours) and ether about $2,220 (down 4%), after an ether low of $2,170, per CoinDesk's Friday report.
Five of the six most-traded bitcoin options are puts (bets on a fall), led by the $74,000 put expiring 13 Nov, per CoinDesk.
BNB fell 6.2% while HYPE rose 15%, per CoinDesk.
Standard Chartered's Geoffrey Kendrick: 'Only after assets are unfrozen and more detail of the hack emerges will we find a new base,' per CoinDesk.

sources.label: CoinDesk: Standard Chartered sees more losses ahead

stories.title: NYSE owner ICE plans regulated US futures based on Hyperliquid
stories.summary: Intercontinental Exchange, which owns the New York Stock Exchange, signed a definitive agreement to be the exclusive operator of Trade[XYZ]'s regulated markets and is taking a strategic stake. It still needs regulatory approval and has no launch date. Hyperliquid's HYPE token kept rising while most of the market fell.
points: US access would come through futures brokers, with distribution via ICE's joint venture with OKX, per Decrypt.
ICE CEO Jeffrey Sprecher called these markets 'additive to our futures markets, not a replacement for them,' per Decrypt.
HYPE rose about 13% to about $91 on Thursday, per Decrypt, and was up 15% in CoinDesk's Friday report.

sources.label: Decrypt via Yahoo: HYPE jumps on ICE deal

briefs.title: Binance went almost an hour without a word as the drain began
briefs.summary: The drain started at 20:24 UTC Thursday; CZ posted at 21:15 UTC and Binance's first statement came at 21:24 UTC. About $628M of positions were force-closed within one hour, per CoinGlass via CryptoTicker.

briefs.title: India's CoinDCX limits futures trading after the Binance incident
briefs.summary: Futures are reduce-only, so no new or bigger positions, citing a global liquidity provider a spokesperson confirmed was Binance. Deposits and withdrawals are unaffected.

briefs.title: Strategy posts a $20.9B profit on bitcoin's rise; its CFO is leaving
briefs.summary: Strategy bought 7,218 BTC and sold 5,552 BTC in Q3 to fund dividends and buybacks. CFO Andrew Kang leaves on 5 Nov, citing personal reasons.

briefs.title: Bitcoin ETF inflows slow to $17.07M
briefs.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs took in $17.07M on 29 Oct, a fourth straight day of inflows but about 88% less than the day before. IBIT took in $12.8M while Grayscale's BTC fund lost $15.35M.

briefs.title: Odds of a December Fed hike fall as stocks slide
briefs.summary: Odds of a December rate hike fell to 70% from nearly 90%; Nasdaq 100 futures were down 2.7% and Intel fell 25%, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Fed held rates at 3.75%-4.00% this week, with two votes for a hike
briefs.summary: The vote on 28 Oct was 10-2; Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack wanted a quarter-point hike.
